name: Hologram AI kernel
purpose: Decides what Hologram AI may load and run. A request names one decision in its first byte and carries that decision's numbers; the answer is the verdict. Seventeen decisions: the next step of the journey (1), whether a model may proceed (2), whether a stage plan is right (3), the quantisation tier (4), whether a buffer is admitted (5), whether a tensor's byte range is valid (6), whether a trim of the conversation is right (7), the next attention cache size (8), a turn's token budget (9), whether an ONNX graph may be imported (10), the size a dimension is bound to (11), which backend can run the model (12), how long one block of weights is (13), whether a token is the first of the highest scores (14), whether a token lies in the penalty window (15), whether a speculative commit is the right size (16) and what a quantisation code stands for (17). Anything else answers invalid request.
placeholder: hex: followed by the decision's bytes

promise.headline: Admits a buffer exactly when its label and its length are the ones expected.
promise.detail: A buffer's label is the BLAKE3 hash of its bytes. The kernel compares all 32 bytes of the expected and observed labels and the declared and observed lengths, and admits only when every one is equal.

claim: KN-05: a buffer is admitted exactly when its expected and observed labels are equal and its declared and observed lengths are equal.

proposition.name: Admitted
proposition.text:
Admitted claim :=
  SameLabel claim.expected claim.observed
  /\ claim.declaredLength = claim.observedLength

SameLabel left right :=
  left.w0 = right.w0 /\ left.w1 = right.w1 /\ left.w2 = right.w2 /\ left.w3 = right.w3
proposition.plain: The observed label is the expected label, word for word, and the observed length is the declared length.
